info.title: bank8-ledger
info.description: Sentin8 Bank8:Ledger - core ledger, posting engine, product library.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/account-migrations` - submit a bulk account migration batch
(Data-Loader-style staging; idempotent re-run via `:bulkRetry`).
`POST /v1/account-plan-assocs` - associate an account with a plan.

`POST /v1/account-update-batches/{id}/bulk-retry` - retry failed rows in a
bulk batch (Sentin8 Jobs bulk-operations pattern). Staged rows are applied
account-by-account; already-applied rows are skipped (idempotent).

parameters.name: env_id
parameters.description: Staff-realm env override for internal-account reads (org-validated)

post.summary:
`POST /v1/accounts` - create account (v1 legacy).
.5: holder callers can only create accounts owned by
themselves. Server-side defence-in-depth:
- If the caller is a holder (§4.3c - no `holder:view-all` scope) and
they did not supply `customer_id`, we resolve it from their Auth
user id (via `customers`).
- If the caller is a holder and they did supply a `customer_id` that
does not match their own, we return 403 (they cannot create
accounts for someone else).
- If no `customers` row exists for the holder, we return 403
- there is no way to own the account, so creating it would leave an
orphan (the list/get handlers then hide it forever).
- Callers with `holder:view-all` (staff / sys / M2M) are
unrestricted: they can pass any `customer_id` or none (for
internal accounts).

400.description: Invalid account type or module validation failed

get.summary:
`GET /v1/accounts/{id}` - account detail.
.5: customer-realm callers can only fetch their own accounts
the service layer verifies the account's `customer_id` matches the
caller's customer before returning. RLS is the backstop.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/adjustments` - create an adjustment: recompute the account state
for backdated postings/parameter changes by re-running the on-schedule
modules from the effective date and submitting a correction batch.

200.description: Adjustment created and applied (correction batch submitted)

get.summary:
`GET /v1/admin/overview` - the overview page's data (accounts-backed
summary; same handler as `GET /v1/accounts`).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/admin/products` - handle product creation form submission.
Called by the RFW form renderer when the user clicks "Create Product".
Creates the product and returns an `AdminUiResponse::redirect` so the
RFW renderer navigates back to the products list.

get.summary: GET /v1/admin/ui/{page} - return RFW definition for the requested admin page.

`GET /v1/contract-modules` - contract module catalog (Func modules
registered per product; sourced from the products' contract_modules field).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/contracts:simulate` - execute a module hook against synthetic
account state . Calls Sentin8:Func `POST /v1/modules/{id}/execute`
with a mock host-function context; **no persistence occurs** - the raw
hook result is returned for preview/dry-run use.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/customers` - list/search customers.
Optional `?search=<text>` filters by display_name or email (case-insensitive
substring match). Without a search term, returns all customers in the
caller's org/env (subject to RLS).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/customers` - create a customer.
If the caller is a user token, the `sentin8_auth_user_id` is stamped
from their token claims so that holder-scoped RLS and
`resolve_caller_customer_id` can find the row.

409.description: Auth user already linked to another customer

get.summary: `GET /v1/dlq` - list dead-letter queue entries (local posting DLQ + Cron schedule DLQ).

post.summary: `POST /v1/flags` - set a flag on an account or customer.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/internal-accounts` - list internal accounts (nickname/product_type
filter). Staff-realm callers may pass the org-validated `?env_id=` override
per tenant-isolation design §10.1 (handled by the shared env resolution).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/internal-accounts` - create an internal account
(counterparty plumbing: cash deposit, clearing, suspense, etc.).

`POST /v1/internal/func-host` - Sentin8:Func proxy-back for host functions.
Authorization: M2M token with `bank8:ledger:postings:write` (the Func
runtime authenticates with the posting service's M2M identity because
host functions can move money). Tenant context comes from the `env_id`
in the request body - the Func runtime resolves it from the hook
context, and the M2M token's own env claim is cross-checked.

post.description:
Authorization mirrors the platform's canonical Flow proxy-back gate
(sys `flow_delegate::execute_step`): the caller must present an
Auth-issued M2M bearer with `sentin8:sys:steps:execute` (Flow's
`sentin8-flow-sys` client). Transport identity (PQ-TLS + platform CA)
is machine identity, not service authorization; anonymous → 401,
wrong scope → 403. The workflow's env is cross-checked against the
bearer's env claim (a proxy-back can only act on an env its token
can address; the platform plane bypasses via `is_platform_admin`).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/journal-events/{id}/replay` - re-drive a journal event
idempotently . The journal row carries the full operation payload;
posting replays are no-ops thanks to posting idempotency keys. Other
resource kinds re-apply the recorded operation.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/parameter-values:viewEffective` - resolve effective parameter value
at a point in time, with hierarchy precedence (account > hierarchy > global).
get.description:
Results are served from a bounded TTL cache (design §10): the
parameter-value write path is insert-only with `effective_from`, so a
short TTL self-heals and no event-driven invalidation is needed. The
posting money path never consults this cache - parameter resolution
there is transactional by design (a stale fee rate is a correctness
defect, not a latency trade).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/plans/{id}/migrations` - migrate accounts onto a plan
(PlanMigration): re-associates the from-plan accounts and closes it.

`POST /v1/post-posting-failures/{id}/republish` - re-run the post-posting
hook for a committed batch (delegates to Sentin8:Func).
`POST /v1/postings/async` - async posting via Bus (enqueues to Bus stream).

`POST /v1/products/{id}/activate` - activate a product.
Also accepts `ledger:write` (broad write scope) for end-user app tokens.
`POST /v1/restriction-sets` - apply a restriction set to an account or customer.

`POST /v1/schedule-tags/{id}/assocs` - attach a tag to a schedule
(tag status ACTIVE/INACTIVE controls the schedule).

`POST /v1/schedules` - create a schedule, delegating execution to Cron.
Ledger stores a local reference in `schedules` and creates the actual
schedule in Cron via `POST /v1/schedules`. Cron fires the schedule and
proxy-calls Ledger's `POST /v1/internal/schedules/run` to execute the work.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/streams` - client-facing streaming catalog: the `event_type`
families the ledger emits on the `bus:{envId}:ledger` stream family
(business "Core Streaming API"; topic mapping in design §11).
`GET /v2/balances/series` - balance series over a time range (bucket scan).

ListAccountsQuery.description:
`GET /v1/accounts` - list accounts.
.5: holder callers (§4.3c - no `holder:view-all` scope) see only
accounts held by their own `customers` row, and only
`account_type='customer'` accounts (internal accounts are never exposed
to holders - forced here in the service layer; RLS is the backstop).
Callers with `holder:view-all` see all env accounts. A holder caller's
`?customer_id=` query param is ignored - they cannot impersonate another
customer.

env_id.description:
§10.1 - staff-realm env override for internal-account reads.
Validated against org membership; ignored for customer/delegated
tokens (env-locked) and never widens customer-data visibility.

Target env_id for the query. Staff tokens carry
env_id = System Env; the caller passes the real env_id here so
the query scopes to the correct environment. Ignored for
holder tokens (they are already env-scoped).

ScheduleRunResponse.description:
`POST /v1/internal/schedules/run` - Cron proxy-back endpoint.
Cron calls this when a Ledger schedule fires. Ledger executes the scheduled
work (§4.3): it resolves the schedule's `schedule_type`, loads the affected
account(s) with their product modules + parameters, runs the on-schedule
module functions to generate posting instructions, and submits them as one
atomic posting batch. A `bank8_ledger_jobs` row records the outcome
`failed` + `error_message` when any step fails (never unconditionally
completed); `last_run_at` is updated only via propagated, awaited writes.
The `POST /v1/internal/schedules/run` reply.
